findings.title: Missing Schema.org Product and Offer structured data on commercial page
findings.evidence: Observed at https://stripe.com/in/pricing via jsonld_schema_extractor [2026-08-31T20:18:16Z]: Commercial/product page (https://stripe.com/in/pricing) contains no Product or Offer structured data to convey machine-readable pricing and features. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Add Schema.org Product and Offer JSON-LD to commercial and pricing pages.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Embed JSON-LD with @type 'Product' or 'Service' and nested 'Offer' elements defining prices, currency, billing cycles, and availability.

evidence_details.observation: Commercial/product page (https://stripe.com/in/pricing) contains no Product or Offer structured data to convey machine-readable pricing and features.

findings.title: No extractable answer on-site for "What does Stripe offer?"
findings.evidence: Observed at https://stripe.com via onsite_answerability_probe [2026-08-31T20:18:27Z]: Across 5 crawled page(s), no Product/Service/Offer schema describes the offering. An assistant that fetched these pages could not quote an answer to "What does Stripe offer?" from this site, so it must fall back to third-party sources or omit the brand. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Mark up the product or service catalogue.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add Product or Service JSON-LD to the pages describing what you sell, so an assistant can quote the offering rather than paraphrasing navigation labels.

evidence_details.observation: Across 5 crawled page(s), no Product/Service/Offer schema describes the offering. An assistant that fetched these pages could not quote an answer to "What does Stripe offer?" from this site, so it must fall back to third-party sources or omit the brand.

findings.title: Multiple competing <h1> headings cause ambiguous page hierarchy
findings.evidence:
Observed at https://stripe.com/in/pricing via heading_structure_inspection [2026-08-31T20:18:16Z]: Page defines 88 separate <h1> tags (; Payments; Revenue), diluting semantic structure. (Confidence: high)
Additional evidence (engagement-audit): Observed at https://stripe.com/in/guides/best-practices-for-launching-and-scaling-platform-payments via heading_structure_inspection [2026-08-31T20:18:16Z]: Page defines 22 separate <h1> tags (; Payments; Revenue), diluting semantic structure. (Confidence: high)
Additional evidence (engagement-audit): Observed at https://stripe.com/in/newsroom/news/stripe-openai-instant-checkout via heading_structure_inspection [2026-08-31T20:18:16Z]: Page defines 19 separate <h1> tags (; Payments; Revenue), diluting semantic structure. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Consolidate heading hierarchy to a single primary <h1>.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Keep one top-level <h1> for the primary topic and convert subordinate headings to <h2> or <h3>.

evidence_details.observation: Page defines 88 separate <h1> tags (; Payments; Revenue), diluting semantic structure.

findings.title: Deep hierarchical page lacks breadcrumb navigation trail
findings.evidence:
Observed at https://stripe.com/in/pricing via breadcrumb_markup_inspector [2026-08-31T20:18:16Z]: Page at deep route (/in/pricing) lacks breadcrumb UI or Schema.org BreadcrumbList markup for parent context. (Confidence: medium)
Additional evidence (engagement-audit): Observed at https://stripe.com/in/contact/sales via breadcrumb_markup_inspector [2026-08-31T20:18:16Z]: Page at deep route (/in/contact/sales) lacks breadcrumb UI or Schema.org BreadcrumbList markup for parent context. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Add breadcrumb navigation trail with BreadcrumbList schema.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add visual breadcrumb navigation and accompanying Schema.org BreadcrumbList JSON-LD to assist user orientation.

evidence_details.observation: Page at deep route (/in/pricing) lacks breadcrumb UI or Schema.org BreadcrumbList markup for parent context.

proactive_recommendations.title: Add BreadcrumbList schema to deep pages
proactive_recommendations.rationale: 4 crawled page(s) sit two or more levels deep with no BreadcrumbList markup. Breadcrumbs give both a visitor arriving cold from an AI answer and the assistant itself the parent context a deep URL otherwise lacks.

suggested_action.summary: Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD alongside visible breadcrumb navigation.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Emit BreadcrumbList JSON-LD listing each ancestor with position, name and item URL, and render the same trail visibly at the top of the page.

proactive_recommendations.title: State AI usage terms explicitly in robots.txt
proactive_recommendations.rationale: robots.txt names which agents may crawl but says nothing about what may be done with the content once fetched. Emerging conventions -- Cloudflare's Content Signals Policy (released CC0) and RSL licensing terms -- let a publisher separate training use from search indexing and answer generation in machine-readable form, instead of leaving that distinction to be inferred from which user agents happen to be listed.

suggested_action.summary: Add machine-readable content-usage signals to robots.txt.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a Content Signals Policy block declaring your position on search, ai-input and ai-train separately, or publish RSL licensing terms. Keep it consistent with the agents you actually allow, or the two signals will contradict each other.

proactive_recommendations.title: Expose an agent-facing endpoint (NLWeb / MCP) built on existing structured data
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site already publishes structured data, which is the input NLWeb uses to serve a conversational endpoint that AI agents can query directly rather than scraping HTML. Because it builds on schema.org markup, sitemaps and feeds you already maintain, it is incremental rather than a rebuild, and it moves the brand from being read by agents to being queryable by them.

suggested_action.summary: Evaluate an NLWeb instance exposing an /ask and /mcp endpoint over existing content.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Point an NLWeb instance at your existing schema.org data and sitemap, and expose /ask and /mcp. Start with the content an agent is most likely to be asked about -- catalogue, docs, pricing.
